turns.text: *Clang.* Something drops two crates over before the ears finish turning toward it — not a footstep, heavier, metal on metal. Body's already down low behind a stacked pallet, still as the crate it's pressed against, breath shallow.

the dock runs four bays deep under a sodium-lit awning, NEKOCORP // PERISHABLE stenciled across four different crate stacks, two guarded by a floodlight rig that never fully turns off. the clang was a loading arm resetting itself between shipments, servo settling wrong the way it has for months. the crates nearest the back bay smell older than the rest — brine gone thick, and under it, something coppery that isn't fish, dried into the pallet wood like it's been there longer than any shipment.

Copper wins over brine, every time — old habit, older than hunger. Slides out from behind the pallet once the loading arm's servo settles fully still, moving low along the back bay's shadow like the ground already belongs to someone who's crossed it a hundred nights running.

the back bay's floodlight flickers on a five-minute delay, plenty of runway. a patrol drone crosses high overhead, its underslung speaker crackling half a jingle before catching itself — not an ad this time, a standing order looped low-volume into every restricted zone in the district: BE ADVISED. UNAUTHORIZED CARGO INTERFERENCE BY SUBJECT DESIGNATE 'KNIFEBOY' CARRIES A STANDING BOUNTY OF 40,000 LOYALTY POINTS. the drone doesn't slow, doesn't look down, just keeps broadcasting the same stale warning to a dock that's heard it a hundred times before.

Doesn't break stride at a number that's been the same for months — points that expire before anyone collects them anyway, not worth the flinch. keeps low along the crate line, nose already committed to the copper-brine thread, ears cataloguing the drone's fade-out overhead.

the thread ends at a crate seam already pried once and re-nailed badly, someone's past work showing through the gaps. inside, three fish gone the deep red-brown of old blood-tinged ice — a shipment that never should have thawed, sabotage or accident, no way to tell which from a cat's side of it. two bays down a guard's boots scrape concrete, unhurried, making a round that hasn't varied in weeks.

Claws find the pried seam's soft edge first, teeth finishing the job fast — one fish, heavy with old ice, worth the drag. doesn't wait to taste it here. grips low and cuts wide of the guard's round, timing the boots' scrape same as any drone's sweep, gone before the concrete finishes its scrape.

the escape route runs along a drainage channel skirting the dock's east wall, quieter than the bay floor by a full register. up on the retaining wall above, another shape sits hunched and twitching at nothing — ears flicking to a sound that isn't there, tongue working like it's tasting the drone's radio chatter instead of hearing it, some other cat's nervous system rewired by somebody's cut-rate lab patch. it doesn't look down. whatever's wrong with it isn't interested in fish.

No interest in whatever's wrong with the shape on the wall — not prey, not threat, just noise wearing fur. Follows the channel to its grate mouth instead, fish gripped tight, and doesn't stop moving until three full turns separate the bounty drone's last broadcast from the sound of its own breathing.

the grate mouth opens onto a service alley two blocks clear of the dock's floodlights, rain starting thin over corrugated roofing, drumming a rhythm indifferent to what just crossed under it. somewhere behind, the standing bounty keeps looping into the restricted zone's dead air, unclaimed, uncollected, same as it's been for longer than anyone still counts.

Settles into the alley's driest corner, fish held down with both paws, and finally starts eating — unhurried now that the dock's floodlights are two blocks of concrete and rain behind. Ears stay up anyway. habit outlives the danger every time.

the alley holds its rain and its quiet in equal measure, roofing drumming steady overhead. two streets over, the dock resets itself for the next scheduled shipment, floodlight rig ticking back to standby, the pried crate seam already flagged for a repair request that will sit in a queue nobody works. the city keeps its books regardless of who's eating well tonight.

Grooms the copper-brine smell off one paw at a time, slow now, no reason left to hurry. Curls down against the dry brick once the last of the fish is gone, tail wrapped tight, eyes closing on the alley's dark rather than fighting it.

rain keeps its rhythm on the roofing long after the eyes close, the district's two rhythms — dock and drone, floodlight and boot-scrape — ticking on somewhere behind the block's quiet, indifferent to the one set of ribs finally resting easy enough to sleep.

Half-wakes at a vibration through the brick — not footsteps, something rolling, slow and heavy, blocks away but felt more than heard. Doesn't fully surface. Files it as far enough to ignore and lets sleep pull back down.

the vibration is a freight hauler two districts over, grinding along its rail same as every other night, nothing aimed at this block. further off still, past where the vibration fades entirely, a stretch of flattened lot holds its silence the way it always does — an old demolition scar nobody's built back over, a vent stack still breathing warm air up from underneath for reasons the district stopped asking about years ago.

Wakes fully when the light through the alley mouth turns the color of old steel rather than none at all. Stretches out the stiffness one leg at a time, tongue working once more over the paw that still smells faintly of brine.

the alley's rain has thinned to a drip off the roofline's low corner, morning traffic starting to hum two streets over. back at the dock, the floodlight rig cycles off for the day shift, a fresh delivery schedule bolted up beside the old one, the pried crate seam still unflagged in any way that matters.

Doesn't head back toward the dock — the ground there's already been claimed enough times tonight. Presses a cheek instead against the alley's corner drainpipe on the way out, layering one more mark over ground that's quietly, unofficially, always been walked the same way.

the mark holds as long as the rain allows, same as every mark in this district ever does. somewhere behind, the standing bounty keeps broadcasting into a restricted zone that's already forgotten it was visited, forty thousand points nobody's closer to collecting than they were the night the number first went up.
